method: DOM text rendered black on white, screenshot, ink = sum of (255 - luminance) per row, relative to 400 in the same face, size and engine. Faces identified by large-glyph ink (100px) and by Chromium's CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode; never by canvas (WebKit canvas skips user-installed fonts) and never from a Chromium fullPage capture (it swaps the generic monospace from Courier to Menlo). Pages carry lang="en", as the report does.

weight_to_ink_percent_vs_400._note: System SF Mono figures are at 11-13 px with the string 'frustration basket total p03 AaGg0O' (400-500) and 'p03 [00:14:32] Login.tsx AaGg0O' (500-700); other strings and sizes move them by 2-5 points, not their order. 'B' means the face's Bold.

weight_matching.mac (both engines): CSS rule: above 500, the next heavier face that exists. Two-instance faces flip to Bold at 501.
weight_matching.windows chromium (DirectWrite): nearest named weight, ties going heavier: Consolas Regular to 540, Bold from 550; Cascadia Regular to 490, SemiBold from 500.
weight_matching.static SF Mono download: 300 and 370 to Light; 420-500 to Medium; 520-600 to Semibold; 700 Bold.

safe_band: Every weight from 400 to 490 renders Regular in Menlo, Courier, Consolas and Cascadia Mono, and varies only in SF Mono. 500 is the first weight that changes another face (Cascadia SemiBold); 550 the first that reaches Consolas Bold.
